# BC Electrical Safety Regulation: Low-Voltage Work Requirements

## Licensed Contractor Requirement

The regulation doesn't explicitly exempt low-voltage work from requiring a licensed electrical contractor. Section 4(1) permits individuals to perform electrical work if they hold appropriate qualifications, including being a "licensed electrical contractor," but doesn't carve out voltage-based exceptions.

## Field Safety Representative (FSR) Requirements

For operating permits involving maintenance, Section 14 states: "the application for the operating permit must include the name, class and certificate of qualification number of the field safety representative who will perform or supervise the regulated work."

Section 16(2) requires utility representatives to provide FSR details but doesn't explicitly prohibit employee FSRs.

## Communication/Low-Voltage Exemptions

**The regulation provides no specific exemption for communications wiring or systems under 30 volts.** The definition of "electrical equipment" in Section 1 is broad: "includes apparatus, conduits, plant, pipes, poles, works and any other regulated product that is used, designed or intended for use for or in connection with the generation, transmission, supply, distribution, or use of electrical energy."

**Recommendation:** Consult with a provincial safety manager to clarify whether specific low-voltage installations qualify for exemptions under Section 18 or the B.C. Electrical Code standards referenced in Section 20.
